result.title: FedSharp: Byzantine Robust Decentralized Federated Learning Under Noisy Channel
result.comment: 6 pages, 4 figures, submitted for possible publication
result.summary: Decentralized federated learning (DFL) eliminates the central aggregation server but remains vulnerable to data heterogeneity, Byzantine attacks, and channel noise. We show that noise accumulates as models propagate across nodes, becoming increasingly significant as the learning rate decays. Moreover, accumulated noise enables Byzantine attackers to exploit loss-based model selection by mimicking honest model averages. To address these challenges, we propose screened, hop-aware, ranked, proximal averaging, a robust DFL framework (FedSharp). In this approach, each node maintains models from its 2b predecessors, ensuring at least b honest candidates when at most b nodes are Byzantine. FedSharp screens suspicious models using coordinate-wise median deviations, averages the b lowest-loss candidates to reduce fresh channel-noise variance by a factor of b, and applies noise-adaptive gradient-norm regularization and proximal training to mitigate accumulated noise and non-IID drift. Experiments on a 100-node ring with 33 Byzantine nodes show that FedSharp achieves 93.5-94.9% accuracy on MNIST, compared with 29.4-38.1% for a state-of-the-art single-model-selection benchmark, and 32.8-48.8% on CIFAR-10, compared with 10.0-30.5%, across Gaussian and hidden attacks under IID and non-IID data. On MNIST, FedSharp also achieves accuracy within approximately one percentage point of the benchmark operating without channel noise.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 FedSharp，一种面向去中心化联邦学习的鲁棒聚合框架：节点保留 2b 个前驱模型，用坐标中位数偏差筛除可疑模型，再对损失最低的 b 个候选做近端平均，并结合噪声自适应梯度范数正则，以应对信道噪声累积、Byzantine 攻击与非 IID 漂移。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作研究分布式训练中的拜占庭鲁棒聚合与信道噪声，不涉及视觉或多模态推理的内部表示、证据使用或推理期状态生成，其模型筛选机制也难以具体对应 LVR 的假设选择问题，故排除。
